title: South America General Knowledge
description: 36 original questions covering the Andes, Amazon, Patagonia, ancient cultures, and landmarks of South America (Multiple Choice & Free-Text).
author: QuizRooms

questions.prompt: Which South American country is the largest by both area and population?
questions.explanation: Brazil covers nearly half of the South American continent.

questions.prompt: Which vast tropical rainforest spans nine South American nations, primarily Brazil?
questions.explanation: The Amazon is the largest tropical rainforest on Earth.

questions.prompt: Which iconic 15th-century Inca citadel sits high in the Peruvian Andes?
questions.explanation: Machu Picchu was built during the reign of Inca emperor Pachacuti.

questions.prompt: What is the longest continental mountain range in the world, running down South America's west coast?
questions.explanation: The Andes stretch over 7,000 kilometers from Venezuela to Chile and Argentina.

questions.prompt: Which iconic Art Deco statue overlooks Rio de Janeiro from Corcovado Mountain?
questions.explanation: Standing 30 meters tall, Christ the Redeemer was completed in 1931.

questions.prompt: Which South American river carries the largest volume of water of any river on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Amazon accounts for roughly one-fifth of all river flow into Earth's oceans.

questions.prompt: Which South American country is famous for tango dancing and Patagonia?
questions.explanation: Tango developed in the working-class neighborhoods of Buenos Aires and Montevideo.

questions.prompt: Which volcanic archipelago belonging to Ecuador inspired Charles Darwin's theory of evolution?
questions.explanation: Darwin visited the Galápagos aboard HMS Beagle in 1835.

questions.prompt: Which South American country is named after the imaginary line dividing Earth's northern and southern hemispheres?
questions.explanation: The equator runs just north of Quito, Ecuador's capital.

questions.prompt: Which long, narrow country stretches along South America's southwestern Pacific coast?
questions.explanation: Chile spans over 4,200 km north-to-south while averaging only 177 km wide.

questions.prompt: Which South American country is famed worldwide for its high-altitude Arabica coffee?
questions.explanation: Colombia's Andean slopes offer ideal volcanic soil and climate for coffee.

questions.prompt: Which domesticated Andean pack animal is closely related to the alpaca?
questions.explanation: Llamas have carried loads across the Andes for thousands of years.

questions.prompt: What is the highest mountain in the Americas and the Western Hemisphere, located in Argentina?
questions.explanation: Aconcagua rises to 6,961 meters in Mendoza Province, Argentina.

questions.prompt: Which waterfall system on the Argentina-Brazil border features over 270 individual drops?
questions.explanation: Iguazu Falls is the largest waterfall system in the world.

questions.prompt: Which Venezuelan waterfall is the tallest uninterrupted waterfall on Earth?
questions.explanation: Angel Falls plunges 979 meters from Auyán-tepui in Canaima National Park.

questions.prompt: Which desert in northern Chile is the driest non-polar desert on Earth?
questions.explanation: Some weather stations in the Atacama have gone decades without measurable rainfall.

questions.prompt: Which high-altitude lake straddling Peru and Bolivia is the highest navigable lake in the world?
questions.explanation: Lake Titicaca sits at 3,812 meters above sea level.

questions.prompt: Which huge salt flat in southwestern Bolivia turns into a giant natural mirror after rain?
questions.explanation: Salar de Uyuni spans over 10,000 square kilometers and holds vast lithium reserves.

questions.prompt: Which South American liberator earned the title 'El Libertador' for leading independence across northern South America?
questions.explanation: Bolivia is named in honor of Simón Bolívar.

questions.prompt: Which two South American countries are completely landlocked?
questions.explanation: Every other sovereign South American country borders an ocean.

questions.prompt: Which Brazilian planned modernist capital was inaugurated in 1960 in the shape of an airplane?
questions.explanation: Oscar Niemeyer and Lúcio Costa designed Brasília's iconic modernist architecture.

questions.prompt: Which vast tropical wetland centered in Brazil is the largest tropical wetland area on Earth?
questions.explanation: The Pantanal is one of the best places in the Americas to spot jaguars.

questions.prompt: Which region at the southern tip of South America is shared by Argentina and Chile?
questions.explanation: Patagonia is famed for glacial peaks, fjords, and windswept steppes.

questions.prompt: Which ancient Peruvian culture created giant desert geoglyphs depicting animals and geometric lines?
questions.explanation: The Nazca Lines were etched into Peru's arid coastal plain between 500 BCE and 500 CE.

questions.prompt: Which Ecuadorian volcano's summit is the farthest point on Earth's surface from the center of the planet?
questions.explanation: Because Earth bulges at the equator, Chimborazo's peak sits farther from Earth's center than Everest.

questions.prompt: Which strait near the southern tip of South America was first navigated by Europeans in 1520?
questions.explanation: Ferdinand Magellan's fleet passed through the strait linking the Atlantic and Pacific.

questions.prompt: Which 1494 treaty divided newly encountered lands outside Europe between Portugal and Spain?
questions.explanation: The Treaty of Tordesillas explains why Brazil speaks Portuguese while its neighbors speak Spanish.

questions.prompt: Which South American country is home to the world's largest single-drop waterfall by volume, Kaieteur Falls?
questions.explanation: Kaieteur Falls drops 226 meters on the Potaro River in Guyana.

questions.prompt: Which grassy plains region in Argentina, Uruguay, and southern Brazil is famed for cattle ranching and gauchos?
questions.explanation: The fertile Pampas cover over 1.2 million square kilometers.

questions.prompt: Which city in southern Peru served as the historic capital of the Inca Empire?
questions.explanation: Cusco's name meant 'navel of the world' in Quechua.

questions.prompt: What is the name of the indigenous knotted-string recording system used by the Inca Empire?
questions.explanation: Quipus recorded census figures, tribute, and accounts using dyed cotton or camelid cords.

questions.prompt: Which active volcano on the Chile-Argentina border is the highest volcano on Earth?
questions.explanation: Ojos del Salado rises to 6,893 meters in the Atacama Andes.

questions.prompt: Which Argentine city on Tierra del Fuego is widely promoted as the southernmost city in the world?
questions.explanation: Ushuaia sits on the Beagle Channel and serves as a gateway to Antarctica.

questions.prompt: Which European spaceport operates in South America near Kourou?
questions.explanation: French Guiana's equatorial location gives rockets an extra rotational boost from Earth.

questions.prompt: Which South American lake in Venezuela is famous for near-continuous nocturnal Catatumbo lightning?
questions.explanation: Catatumbo lightning flashes over Lake Maracaibo more nights per year than almost anywhere else.

questions.prompt: Which remote Pacific island famous for its moai stone statues is a special territory of Chile?
questions.explanation: Known locally as Rapa Nui, Easter Island lies over 3,500 km west of mainland Chile.
